title: MARC 21 Format for Community Information as of Update No. 35
description: MARC 21 Format for Community Information, derived from the Library of Congress documentation as of Update No. 35.

LDR.label: Leader
LDR.description:
Fixed field that comprises the first 24 character positions (00-23) of each record and provides information for the processing of the record.

Consists of data elements that contain numbers or coded values that define the parameters for the processing of the record. Character positions 20-23 comprise the Entry map for the Directory. They contain four one-character numbers that specify the structure of the entries in the Directory. More detailed information about the structure of the Leader is contained in MARC 21 Specifications for Record Structure, Character Sets, and Exchange Media .

00-04.label: Record length
00-04.description: Five-character number equal to the length of the entire record, including itself and the record terminator. The number is right justified and unused positions contain zeros.

05.label: Record status
05.description: Relationship of the record to a file for file maintenance purposes.

c.label: Corrected or revised
c.description: Addition or change has been made to the record.

n.label: New
n.description: Record is a newly input record.

06.label: Type of record
06.description: Characteristics and definitions of the components of the record.

q.label: Community information
q.description: Record constitutes a community information record. Community information records describe non-bibliographic resources that fulfill the information needs of a community. The kind of data found in the community information record is identified by the code in Leader/07.

07.label: Kind of data
07.description: Kind of data found in the record.

n.label: Individual
n.description: Individual with a particular expertise (e.g., teacher, interpreter, storyteller, civic leader).

o.label: Organization
o.description: Organization or any group (e.g., corporation, association, club, agency).

p.label: Program or service
p.description:
Offering or activity of a group or institution which carries out the the organization's purpose.

Examples include driver education, day care placement, toy collection drive, blood bank.

q.label: Event
q.description: Scheduled happening (e.g., a lecture, play, concert series, sporting contest, festival, annual celebration, regularly scheduled meeting).

z.label: Other
z.description:
Entity other than those specified by the other defined codes (e.g., a facility such as a planetarium on a university campus.

Note that separate records are not created for equipment. Information about equipment available from a community information entity that is to be used at the entity is recorded in subfield $e (Equipment Available) of field 311 (Meeting Rooms and Facilities Available); information about equipment available from a community information entity that may be used outside of the entity is recorded in field 312 (Equipment Available).

09.label: Character coding scheme
09.description:
Character coding scheme used in the record.

Coding scheme used affects the number of octets needed per character, the placement of non-spacing characters, and the use of escape sequences and may affect the character repertoire. Detailed information on the character sets used in MARC 21 records is contained in MARC 21 Specifications for Record Structure, Character Sets, and Exchange Media .

.label: MARC-8
.description: Character coding in the record uses the 8-bit character sets described in MARC 21 Specifications for Record Structure, Character Sets, and Exchange Media . Non-default character sets used are identified in field 066.

a.label: UCS/Unicode
a.description: Character coding in the record makes use of characters from the Universal Coded Character Set (UCS) (ISO 10646), or Unicode™, an industry subset.

10.label: Indicator count
10.description:
Computer-generated number 2 that indicates the number of character positions used for indicators in a variable data field.

(An indicator character position contains a code which conveys information that interprets or supplements the data found in the field.) In MARC, two character positions at the beginning of each variable data field are reserved for indicators; therefore, the Indicator count is always 2.

2.label: Number of character positions used for indicators

11.label: Subfield code length
11.description:
Computer-generated number 2 that indicates the number of character positions used for each subfield code in a variable data field.

(Each data element in a variable data field is identified by a subfield code.) In MARC 21, a subfield code consists of a delimiter ($) and a lowercase alphabetic or numeric data element identifier; therefore, the Subfield code count is always 2.

2.label: Number of character positions used for a subfield code

12-16.label: Base address of data
12-16.description:
Computer-generated, five-character numeric string that indicates the first character position of the first variable control field in a record. The number is right justified and each unused position contains a zero.

The number is the base from which the starting character position of all the other fields in the record is addressed in the Directory. (The starting character position in the Directory entry for each field of the record is relative to the first character of the first variable control field rather than the beginning of the record.) The Base address of data is equal to the sum of the lengths of the Leader and the Directory, including the field terminator character at the end of the Directory.

17-19.label: Undefined character positions
17-19.description: Undefined three character positions; each contains a blank (#).

4.label: Number of characters in the length-of-field portion of a Directory entry

5.label: Number of characters in the starting-character-position portion of a Directory entry

22.label: Length of the implementation-defined portion
22.description:
Always contains a 0.

In MARC 21, a Directory entry does not contain an implementation-defined portion.

0.label: Number of characters in the implementation-defined portion of a Directory entry

001.label: Control Number
001.description:
Control number assigned by the organization creating, using, or distributing the record. The organization is identified by the MARC code contained in field 003 (Control Number Identifier).

For interchange purposes, documentation of the structure of the control number and input conventions should be provided to exchange partners by the organization initiating the interchange. An organization receiving a record may move the incoming control number from field 001 (and the control number identifier from field 003) to field 035 (System Control Number), 010 (Library of Congress Control Number), or 016 (National Bibliographic Agency Control Number, as appropriate, and place its own system control number in field 001 (and its control number identifier in field 003).

003.label: Control Number Identifier
003.description:
MARC code for the agency whose system control number is present in field 001 (Control Number).

See Appendix G Organization Code Sources for a listing of organization code sources used in MARC 21 records.

Whenever the number in field 001 is changed, agencies must assure that the MARC code in field 003 applies to the number found in the 001 field.

005.label: Date and Time of Latest Transaction
005.description:
Sixteen characters that indicate the date and time of the latest record transaction and serve as a version identifier for the record. They are recorded according to Representation of Dates and Times (ISO 8601). The date requires 8 numeric characters in the pattern yyyymmdd. The time requires 8 numeric characters in the pattern hhmmss.f, expressed in terms of the 24-hour (00-23) clock.

The date on which a record is first entered into machine-readable form is contained in field 008/00-05. The Date entered on file never changes.

007.label: Physical Description Fixed Field-General Information
007.description:
Eleven character positions (00-09) that contain positionally-defined, coded data elements that describe accommodations provided for people with disabilities. Each defined character position contains either a code or a fill character (|). Code n (Not applicable), when it is defined for a data element, indicates that the character position definition does not apply to the entity. Physical accommodations information may be described textually in field 575 (Accommodations for the Disabled Note).

A fill character may be used in a particular character position when the creator of the record has decided not to attempt to supply a defined code.

00.label: Category
00.description: Category of persons to which the information in field 007 pertains.

e.label: Disabled
e.description: Data in the field pertain to the disabled. The phrase disabled, with respect to an individual, means 1) a physical or mental impairment that substantially limits one or more of the major life activities of the individual; 2) a record of such an impairment; or 3) being regarded as having such an impairment.

01.label: Stairway ramps
01.description: Whether entrance and internal stairway ramps are provided.

a.label: No ramps
a.description: No stairway ramps at the entrance or internally.

b.label: Entrance and internal ramps
b.description: Stairway ramps are at the entrance and internally.

c.label: Entrance ramp only-multiple floors
c.description: Stairway ramp is at the entrance but there are no internal ramps between the floors in the facility.

d.label: Entrance ramp only-single floor
d.description: Stairway ramp is at the entrance but there are no internal ramps because the building is on one floor.

e.label: Internal ramps only
e.description: Internal stairway ramps but no ramp at the entrance.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Ramps information is not applicable to the community information entity involved.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: It is not known whether there are ramps.

02.label: Doors
02.description:
Whether or not the doors accommodate wheelchairs.

Doors may be widened or offset hinges installed.

a.label: No wide or offset-hinge doors
a.description: Doors have not been widened or offset hinges installed.

b.label: Wide or offset-hinge doors
b.description: Doors have been widened or offset hinges installed.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Widened door or offset hinge installation information is not applicable to the community information entity involved.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: It is not known whether the doors have been widened or offset hinges installed.

03.label: Furniture, equipment, display racks
03.description: Whether or not the furniture, equipment, and display racks accommodate people with disabilities.

a.label: Unaccessible furniture, equipment, display racks
a.description: Furniture, equipment, and display racks have not been arranged to meet the needs of people with disabilities.

b.label: Accessible furniture, equipment, display racks
b.description: Furniture, equipment, and display racks have been arranged to meet the needs of people with disabilities.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Arrangement of furniture, equipment, and display racks information pertaining to people with disabilities is not applicable to the community information entity involved.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: It is not known whether the furniture, equipment, and display racks have been arranged to meet the needs of people with disabilities.

04.label: Restrooms
04.description: Whether the restrooms accommodate people with disabilities. Special restroom accommodations include widened toilet stalls, raised toilet seats, and grab bars in toilet stalls.

a.label: No special restroom accommodations or grab bars
a.description: No special restroom accommodations or grab bars in toilet stalls.

b.label: Special restroom accommodations and grab bars

c.label: Special restroom accommodations only
c.description: Special restroom accommodations but no grab bars.

d.label: Grab bars only
d.description: Grab bars but no special restroom accommodations.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Restroom information is not applicable to the community information entity involved.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: It is not known whether there are special restroom facilities and grab bars in toilet stalls.

05.label: Elevators
05.description: Whether the elevators accommodate people with disabilities. Special elevators are those wide enough to accommodate wheelchairs or the elevator control buttons may have raised letters or braille markings on them.

a.label: No special elevators or control buttons
a.description: No special elevators to accommodate wheelchairs and elevator control buttons have no raised letters or braille markings on them.

b.label: Special elevators and control buttons
b.description: Special elevators to accommodate wheelchairs and elevator control buttons have raised letters or braille markings on them.

c.label: Special elevators only
c.description: Special elevators to accommodate wheelchairs but elevator control buttons have no raised letters or braille markings on them.

d.label: Special control buttons only
d.description: Elevator control buttons have raised letters or braille markings on them but there are no special elevators to accommodate wheelchairs.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Elevator information is not applicable to the community information entity involved.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: It is not known whether there are special elevators to accommodate wheelchairs and whether the elevator control buttons have raised letters or braille markings on them.

06.label: Telephones
06.description:
Whether or not the telephones accommodate people with disabilities

Telephones may have been lowered or have handset amplifiers available.

a.label: No lowered telephones or handset amplifiers

b.label: Lowered telephones and handset amplifiers
b.description: Telephones have been lowered and handset amplifiers are available.

c.label: Lowered telephones only
c.description: Telephones have been lowered but no handset amplifiers are available.

d.label: Handset amplifiers only
d.description: There are handset amplifiers available but the telephones have not been lowered.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Lowered telephones and handset amplifiers information is not applicable to the community information entity involved.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: It is not known whether telephones have been lowered and whether handset amplifiers are available.

07.label: Flashing emergency lights
07.description: Whether or not flashing emergency lights have been installed to accommodate people with disabilities.

b.label: Flashing emergency lights
b.description: Flashing emergency lights have been installed.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Flashing emergency lights information is not applicable to the community information entity involved.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: It is not known whether flashing emergency lights have been installed.

08.label: Sign language
08.description: Whether sign language is used to accommodate people with disabilities.

a.label: No sign language
a.description: Sign language is not used at the community information entity.

b.label: Sign language
b.description: Sign language is used at the community information entity.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Sign language information is not applicable to the community information entity involved.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: It is not known whether sign language is used at the community information entity.

09.label: Subtitles and/or supertitles
09.description: Whether or not subtitles and/or supertitles are available at the community information entity to accommodate people with disabilities.

b.label: Subtitles and supertitles
b.description: Subtitles and supertitles are available.

c.label: Subtitles only
c.description: Subtitles, but not supertitles, are available.

d.label: Supertitles only
d.description: Supertitles, but not subtitles, are available.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Subtitles and supertitles information is not applicable to the community information entity involved.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: It is not known whether subtitles and/or supertitles are available.

10.label: Parking
10.description: Availability of parking for the handicapped including vehicles with special height requirements.

b.label: Handicapped accessible parking available with high clearance for special vehicles
b.description: Parking spaces are available for handicapped access in areas, either covered or in open air, that do not present obstacles to vehicles with special height requirements. High clearance is defined as 114 inches, which accommodates all raised roof vans.

c.label: Handicapped accessible parking available with low clearance only
c.description: Handicapped accessible parking spaces are available but they cannot be accessed by vehicles requiring high clearance due to either indoor (e.g., low ceiling) or outdoor (e.g., anti-RV arches) obstacles.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Parking availability information is not applicable to the community information entity involved.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: It is not known whether parking for the handicapped is available.

00-05.label: Date entered on file
00-05.description:
Computer-generated, six-character numeric stringthat indicates the date the MARC record was created. The date is recorded in the pattern yymmdd.

Use yy for the year, mm for the month, and dd for the day). The date entered on file in 008/00-05 is never changed. The date and time of latest transaction information in field 005 changes each time a transaction is made to the record. The latest transaction information enables an organization handling more than one version of a record to identify the most current version.

06.label: Volunteer opportunities
06.description:
Whether opportunities for volunteers are available. This information may be described textually in field 571 (Volunteers Note),first indicator value 0 (Opportunities).

Volunteers are usually expected to go through some training in order to serve and usually have to agree to serve a certain number of hours, etc.

b.label: Volunteer opportunities
b.description: Volunteer opportunities are available.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Volunteer opportunities information is not applicable to the community information entity involved.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: It is not known whether there are volunteer opportunities.

07.label: Volunteers provided
07.description: Whether the services of volunteers are provided. This information may be described textually in field 571 (Volunteers Note), first indicator value 1 (Services provided).

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Volunteers provided information is not applicable to the community information entity involved.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: It is not known whether volunteers are provided.

08.label: Child care arrangements
08.description: Whether child care is provided. This information may be described textually in field 576 (Services Available Note), first indicator value 0 (Child care arrangements).

b.label: Child care arrangements
b.description: Child care arrangements are provided.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Child care arrangements information is not applicable to the community information entity involved.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: It is not known whether there are child care arrangements.

09.label: Speakers bureau
09.description: Whether speakers are available. This information may be described textually in field 576 (Services Available Note), first indicator value 1 (Speakers bureau).

b.label: Speakers bureau
b.description: Speakers bureau is available.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Speakers bureau information is not applicable to the community information entity involved.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: It is not known whether there is a speakers bureau.

10.label: Mutual support groups
10.description: Whether meetings of informal groups to discuss specific concerns are available. This information may be described textually in field 576 (Services Available Note), first indicator value 2 (Mutual support groups).

b.label: Mutual support groups
b.description: Mutual support groups are available.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Mutual support information is not applicable to the community information entity involved.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: It is not known whether there are mutual support groups.

11.label: Meeting rooms and facilities available
11.description:
Whether rooms or other facilities are available. This information may be described textually in field 311 (Meeting Rooms and Facilities Available).

Facilities include swimming pools, bowling alleys, and theaters.

b.label: Meeting rooms and facilities
b.description: Meeting rooms and facilities are available for use.

n.label: Not applicable
n.description: Meeting rooms and facilities information is not applicable to the community information entity involved.

u.label: Unknown
u.description: It is not known whether meeting rooms and facilities are available for use by others.

12-14.label: Language
12-14.description:
Three-character MARC code that indicates the language associated with the community information entity. Code from: MARC Code List for Languages. When more than one language is associated with the entity, all appropriate codes are given in field 041 (Language Code) and the predominant language code is recorded in 008/12-14. Language information may be described textually in field 546 (Language Note).

When there is more than one language, the code recorded in 008/12-14 must always be the same as the first code in field 041, subfield $a. When there is only one language associated with the community information entity, the code for that language is recorded. If there is no predominant language associated with the community information entity, the codes are recorded in English alphabetical order in field 041, and the first one is recorded in 008/12-14.

010.label: Library of Congress Control Number
010.description:
Unique number assigned to a MARC record by the Library of Congress.

The control number for MARC records distributed by LC is referred to as an LC control number (LCCN).

The LC control number is carried in field 001 (Control Number) in records distributed by LC's Cataloging Distribution Service and in field 010 subfield $a. An organization using LC records may remove the LC control number from field 001 and use field 001 for its own system control number.

An LC record may contain field 010 with a canceled or invalid control number of a previously-distributed record. A record may be canceled because it is a duplicate record for the same item. The structure of the canceled/invalid control number is the same as that used by LC in field 001.

a.label: LC control number
a.description: Valid LC control number (see explanation of structure of this number given below).

z.label: Canceled/invalid LC control number
z.description: Canceled or invalid LC control number, including invalid NUCMC numbers.

8.label: Field link and sequence number
8.description:
Data that identifies linked fields and may also propose a sequence for the linked fields. Subfield $8 may be repeated to link a field to more than one other group of fields. The structure and syntax for the field link and sequence number subfield is:

$8[linking number].[sequence number]\[field link type]

Linking number is the first data element in the subfield and required if the subfield is used. It is a variable-length whole number that occurs in subfield $8 in all fields that are to be linked. Fields with the same linking number are considered linked.

Sequence number is separated from linking number by a period "." and is optional. It is a variable- length whole number that may be used to indicate the relative order for display of the linked fields (lower sequence numbers displaying before higher ones). If it is used it must occur in all $8 subfields containing the same linking number.

Field link type is separated from preceding data by a reverse slash "\". It is a code indicating the reason for the link and it follows the link number, or sequence number if present. The following one-character field link type codes have been defined for use in subfield $8:

p.label: Metadata provenance
p.description: Used in a record to link a field with another field containing information about provenance of the metadata recorded in the linked field.

u.label: General linking, type unspecified
u.description: Used in cases when a specific link type is not appropriate. Code “u” may serve as a default value when there is no information about the reason for the link available.

016.label: National Bibliographic Agency Control Number
016.description:
Unique numbers that have been assigned to a record by a national bibliographic agency other than the Library of Congress.

(Library of Congress control numbers are recorded in field 010.) The control number may also appear in field 001 (Control Number) in records distributed by the same national agency. An organization using the record may remove the national bibliographic agency control number from field 001 and use field 001 for its own system control number.

A record may contain field 016 with a canceled or invalid control number of a previously-distributed record. A record may be canceled because it is a duplicate record for the same item.

indicator1.label: National bibliographic agency
indicator1.description: Value that either identifies a specific national bibliographic agency as the source of the control number, or refers to a code in subfield $2 (Source).

.label: Library and Archives Canada
.description: Library and Archives Canada (LAC) is the source of the national bibliographic agency control number.

7.label: Source specified in subfield $2
7.description: Source of the control number is indicated by a code in subfield $2.

a.label: Record control number
a.description: Valid record control number assigned by a national bibliographic agency.

z.label: Canceled or invalid control number
z.description: Canceled or invalid control number assigned by a national bibliographic agency.

2.label: Source
2.description:
MARC code or the name of the organization that identifies the national bibliographic agency that was the source of the record control number recorded in field 016. See MARC Code List for Organizations for a listing of organization code sources used in MARC 21 records.

Used only when the second indicator position contains value 7 (Source specified in subfield $2).

8.label: Field link and sequence number
8.description:
Data that identifies linked fields and may also propose a sequence for the linked fields. Subfield $8 may be repeated to link a field to more than one other group of fields. The structure and syntax for the field link and sequence number subfield is:

$8[linking number].[sequence number]\[field link type]

Linking number is the first data element in the subfield and required if the subfield is used. It is a variable-length whole number that occurs in subfield $8 in all fields that are to be linked. Fields with the same linking number are considered linked.

Sequence number is separated from linking number by a period "." and is optional. It is a variable- length whole number that may be used to indicate the relative order for display of the linked fields (lower sequence numbers displaying before higher ones). If it is used it must occur in all $8 subfields containing the same linking number.

Field link type is separated from preceding data by a reverse slash "\". It is a code indicating the reason for the link and it follows the link number, or sequence number if present. The following one-character field link type codes have been defined for use in subfield $8:

p.label: Metadata provenance
p.description: Used in a record to link a field with another field containing information about provenance of the metadata recorded in the linked field.

u.label: General linking, type unspecified
u.description: Used in cases when a specific link type is not appropriate. Code “u” may serve as a default value when there is no information about the reason for the link available.

035.label: System Control Number
035.description:
System control number for a record that belongs to a system other than the one whose number is contained in field 001 (Control Number), field 010 (Library of Congress Control Number), or field 016 (National Bibliographic Agency Control Number).

For interchange purposes, documentation of the structure and use of the system control number must be provided to exchange partners by the originating organization. Each valid system control number and any related canceled/invalid control number are contained in a separate 035 field.

a.label: System control number
a.description: MARC code (enclosed in parentheses) of the organization originating the system control number, followed immediately by the number. See Organization Code Sources for a listing of organization code sources used in MARC 21 records.

z.label: Canceled/invalid system control number
z.description: Canceled or invalid system control number that is associated with the valid system control number contained in subfield $a.

6.label: Linkage
6.description:
Data that links fields that are different script representations of each other. Subfield $6 may contain the tag number of an associated field, an occurrence number, a code that identifies the first script encountered in a left-to-right scan of the field, and an indication that the orientation for a display of the field data is right-to-left. A regular (non-880) field may be linked to one or more 880 fields that all contain different script representations of the same data. Subfield $6 is structured as follows:

$6[linking tag]-[occurrence number]/[script identification code]/[field orientation code]

Subfield $6 is always the first subfield in the field.

Descriptions of multiscript records, with examples, are in Appendix C of the MARC 21 Format for Community Information; specifications for field 880 are under that field; specifications for character sets and repertoires for scripts are found in MARC 21 Specifications for Record Structure, Character Sets, and Exchange Media.

Linking tag part contains the tag number of the associated field. This part is followed immediately by a hyphen and the two-digit occurrence number part. A different occurrence number is assigned to each set of associated fields within a single record. The function of an occurrence number is to permit the matching of the associated fields (not to sequence the fields within the record). An occurrence number may be assigned at random for each set of associated fields. An occurrence number of less than two digits is right justified and the unused position contains a zero.

When there is no associated field to which a field 880 is linked, the occurrence number in subfield $6 is 00. It is used if an agency wants to separate scripts in a record. The linking tag part of subfield $6 will contain the tag that the associated regular field would have had if it had existed in the record.

Occurrence number is followed immediately by a slash (/) and the script identification code. This code identifies the alternate script found in the field. The following codes are used:

These codes have been defined based on the MARC-8 coded character set escape sequences defined in accordance with ISO IEC 2022, "Character Code Structure and Extension Techniques" (equivalent to ANSI X3.41, "Code Extension Techniques for Use with 7-bit and 8-bit Character Sets"). The codes are described in MARC character set documentation.

In a Unicode environment, script identification codes may instead be taken from ISO 15924 "Codes for the representation of names of scripts". Either the alphabetic values (consisting of four letters) or the numerical values (consisting of three digits) may be used.

Entire field need not be in the script identified in subfield $6. If more than one script is present in the field, subfield $6 will contain the identification of the first alternate script encountered in a left-to-right scan of the field.

Note also that the script identification code is used in field 880, subfield $6, but this data element is not generally used for subfield $6 of the associated regular field. In the associated field, the data is assumed to be the primary script(s) for the record.

In a MARC record, the contents of field 880 are always recorded in their logical order, from the first character to the last, regardless of field orientation. For a display of the field, the default field orientation is left-to-right. When the field contains text that has a right-to-left orientation, the script identification code is followed by a slash (/) and the field orientation code. The MARC field orientation code for right-to-left scripts is the letter r. The orientation code is only included in fields with right-to-left orientation, since left-to-right orientation is the default orientation in 880 fields. (See MARC 21 Specifications for Record Structure, Character Sets, and Exchange Media for a detailed description of field orientation.)

Note that the orientation code is used in field 880, subfield $6, but this data element is not generally used for subfield $6 of the associated regular field. In the associated field, the data is assumed to be the usual orientation of the primary script(s) for the record.

8.label: Field link and sequence number
8.description:
Data that identifies linked fields and may also propose a sequence for the linked fields. Subfield $8 may be repeated to link a field to more than one other group of fields. The structure and syntax for the field link and sequence number subfield is:

$8[linking number].[sequence number]\[field link type]

Linking number is the first data element in the subfield and required if the subfield is used. It is a variable-length whole number that occurs in subfield $8 in all fields that are to be linked. Fields with the same linking number are considered linked.

Sequence number is separated from linking number by a period "." and is optional. It is a variable- length whole number that may be used to indicate the relative order for display of the linked fields (lower sequence numbers displaying before higher ones). If it is used it must occur in all $8 subfields containing the same linking number.

Field link type is separated from preceding data by a reverse slash "\". It is a code indicating the reason for the link and it follows the link number, or sequence number if present. The following one-character field link type codes have been defined for use in subfield $8:

p.label: Metadata provenance
p.description: Used in a record to link a field with another field containing information about provenance of the metadata recorded in the linked field.

u.label: General linking, type unspecified
u.description: Used in cases when a specific link type is not appropriate. Code “u” may serve as a default value when there is no information about the reason for the link available.

040.label: Record Source
040.description:
MARC code or the name of the organization(s) that created the original record, assigned MARC content designation and transcribed the record into machine-readable form, or modified an existing MARC record. See Organization Code Sources for a listing of organization code sources used in MARC 21 records.

MARC codes or names in field 040 specify the responsible parties for the content, content designation, and transcription of a community information record.

a.label: Originating agency
a.description: MARC code or the name of the organization that created the original record.

b.label: Language code
b.description: MARC code for the language used in the textual portion of the record in the Note fields (5XX). Code from: MARC Code List for Languages .

c.label: Transcribing agency
c.description: MARC code or the name of the organization that transcribed the record into machine-readable form. If a transcribing agency also modifies the record in the process of transcribing it, the agency's MARC code or name is also recorded in subfield $d.

d.label: Modifying agency

A modification is defined as any correction to a record, including data, content designation, or keying changes. The MARC code or the name of each organization that modifies a record is contained in a separate subfield $d. Subfield $d is not repeated when the same MARC code or name would occur in adjacent $d subfields. If the same agency transcribing the record also modifies the cataloging record in the process of transcribing it, the agency’s name or MARC code is also recorded in subfield $d.

6.label: Linkage
6.description:

$6[linking tag]-[occurrence number]/[script identification code]/[field orientation code]

Subfield $6 is always the first subfield in the field.

A different occurrence number is assigned to each set of associated fields within a single record. An occurrence number may be assigned at random for each set of associated fields. An occurrence number of less than two digits is right justified and the unused position contains a zero.

The linking tag part of subfield $6 will contain the tag that the associated regular field would have had if it had existed in the record.

Occurrence number is followed immediately by a slash (/) and the script identification code. This code identifies the alternate script found in the field. The following codes are used:

These codes have been defined based on the MARC-8 coded character set escape sequences defined in accordance with ISO IEC 2022, "Character Code Structure and Extension Techniques" (equivalent to ANSI X3.41, "Code Extension Techniques for Use with 7-bit and 8-bit Character Sets"). The codes are described in MARC character set documentation.

$8[linking number].[sequence number]\[field link type]

p.label: Metadata provenance
p.description: Used in a record to link a field with another field containing information about provenance of the metadata recorded in the linked field.

u.label: General linking, type unspecified
u.description: Used in cases when a specific link type is not appropriate. Code “u” may serve as a default value when there is no information about the reason for the link available.

041.label: Language Code
041.description:
Codes for languages associated with the community information entity when the language code in field 008/12-14 (Language) is insufficient for a multilingual entity. Codes from: MARC Code List for Languages or other code lists, such as ISO 639-1 (Codes for the representation of names of languages -- Part 1: alpha-2 code).

In records for organizations or agencies (Leader/07, code o) and programs or services (Leader/07, code p), the language associated with the community information entity is the language spoken by the staff; for individuals (Leader/07, code n) and events (Leader/07, code q), the language is that spoken by the individual or by those participating in the event.

indicator1.label: Translation indication
indicator1.description: Value that specifies whether the language is a translation.

.label: No information provided
.description: No information is provided as to whether the entity is or includes a translation.

0.label: Not translation
0.description: Language of the community information entity is not a translation.

1.label: Translation
1.description: Language of the community information entity is a translation.

indicator2.label: Source of code
indicator2.description: Source of the language code used in the field.

.label: MARC language code
.description: Code from: MARC Code List for Languages .

7.label: Source specified in subfield $2
7.description: Source of the language code is indicated by a code in subfield $2.

a.label: Language code associated with community information entity
a.description: Codes for languages associated with the community information entity. The first language code in subfield $a is also contained in field 008/12-14.

b.label: Language code of supertitle or subtitle
b.description: Codes for languages of supertitles or subtitles when the language of the supertitle or subtitle is other than that associated with the community information entity.

h.label: Language code of original
h.description: Codes for languages of the original.

2.label: Source of code
2.description:
Code that identifies the source of the language code scheme used in the field. Code from: Language Code and Term Source Codes . If a non-MARC code is used to express the predominate language in an item, field 008/12-14 is coded with three fill characters (| | |).

2.description:

.label: Library of Congress Classification

1.label: U.S. Dept. of Defense Classification
1.description: Geographic classification code is from the U.S. Department of Defense Classification system.

7.label: Source specified in subfield $2

p.label: Metadata provenance
p.description: Used in a record to link a field with another field containing information about provenance of the metadata recorded in the linked field.

u.label: General linking, type unspecified
u.description: Used in cases when a specific link type is not appropriate. Code “u” may serve as a default value when there is no information about the reason for the link available.

082.label: Dewey Decimal Classification Number
082.description: Classification number that is assigned from the Dewey Decimal Classification, accessed through electronic or printed versions.

indicator1.label: Type of edition
indicator1.description: Indicates the edition from which the Dewey Decimal classification is taken.

0.label: Full edition
0.description: Class number was taken from the full edition.

1.label: Abridged edition
1.description: Class number was taken from the abridged edition.

7.label: Other edition specified in subfield $2
7.description: The edition is specified in subfield $2 (Edition information).

indicator2.label: Source of call number
indicator2.description: Value that indicates whether the source of the class number is the Library of Congress or another organization.

.label: No information provided
.description: No information is provided about the source of the class number.

0.label: Assigned by LC
0.description: Source of the class number is the Library of Congress. Also used by organizations transcribing from LC copy.

4.label: Assigned by agency other than LC
4.description: Source of the class number is an organization other than the Library of Congress.

b.label: Item number
b.description: Item number portion of a call number.

m.label: Standard or optional designation
m.description: Whether the classification number contained in the field is from the standard or optional part of the schedules or tables of the scheme identified by the first indicator (Type of edition) and by subfield $2 (Edition information). The following codes are used: a (standard) and b (optional).

q.label: Assigning agency
q.description:
MARC organization code of the institution that assigned the classification number.

Code from: MARC Code List for Organizations .

2.label: Edition information
2.description: Information on the edition from which the DDC number was assigned. 6.description:

$6[linking tag]-[occurrence number]/[script identification code]/[field orientation code]

Subfield $6 is always the first subfield in the field.

The linking tag part of subfield $6 will contain the tag that the associated regular field would have had if it had existed in the record.

Occurrence number is followed immediately by a slash (/) and the script identification code. This code identifies the alternate script found in the field. The following codes are used:

These codes have been defined based on the MARC-8 coded character set escape sequences defined in accordance with ISO IEC 2022, "Character Code Structure and Extension Techniques" (equivalent to ANSI X3.41, "Code Extension Techniques for Use with 7-bit and 8-bit Character Sets"). The codes are described in MARC character set documentation.

084.description:

2.description: MARC code for the source of the classification system or scheme from which the number was assigned. Code from: Classification Scheme Source Codes .

c.label: Titles and other words associated with a name
c.description:
Titles and other words associated with a name, including qualifying information such as:

Fuller forms of names given in parentheses are given in subfield $q.

e.label: Relator term
e.description:

g.label: Miscellaneous information
g.description: Data element that is not more appropriately contained in another defined subfield.

j.label: Attribution qualifier

q.label: Fuller form of name

indicator1.description: Undefined and contains a blank (#).

$8[linking number].[sequence number]\[field link type]

Linking number is the first data element in the subfield and required if the subfield is used. It is a variable-length whole number that occurs in subfield $8 in all fields that are to be linked. Fields with the same linking number are considered linked.

Sequence number is separated from linking number by a period "." and is optional. It is a variable- length whole number that may be used to indicate the relative order for display of the linked fields (lower sequence numbers displaying before higher ones). If it is used it must occur in all $8 subfields containing the same linking number.

Field link type is separated from preceding data by a reverse slash "\". It is a code indicating the reason for the link and it follows the link number, or sequence number if present. The following one-character field link type codes have been defined for use in subfield $8:

p.label: Metadata provenance
p.description: Used in a record to link a field with another field containing information about provenance of the metadata recorded in the linked field.

u.label: General linking, type unspecified
u.description: Used in cases when a specific link type is not appropriate. Code “u” may serve as a default value when there is no information about the reason for the link available.

270.label: Address
270.description: Address (as well as electronic access data such as telephone, fax, TTY, etc. number) associated with the community information. Multiple addresses, such as mailing address and address corresponding to the physical location of a resource or facility, are recorded in separate occurrences of field 270.

indicator1.label: Level
indicator1.description: Level of the address which distinguishes between primary and additional (secondary) address.

.label: No level specified
.description: Level of the address could be determined but is not specified.

1.label: Primary
1.description: Information relates to a primary address.

2.label: Secondary
2.description: Address that is not the primary address.

indicator2.label: Type of address
indicator2.description: Type of the address for cases when identification of the type is needed at the field level. At present, only one type of address is accommodated by a specific second indicator value. Other types may be indicated in subfield $i (Type of address).

.label: No type specified
.description: Type of address could be determined but is not specified.

0.label: Mailing
0.description: Mailing address.

7.label: Type specified in subfield $i
7.description: Address is other than a mailing address and that its type is identified in subfield $i (Type of address).

a.label: Address
a.description:
Address information preceding the name of the city or town, except attention information which is recorded in subfields $f, $g, and $h. It can also contain information indicating that no address information is available.

Subfield $a repeatability permits multiline display of the address.

b.label: City
b.description: Name of the city or town.

c.label: State or province
c.description: Name of the state, province, or next larger jurisdiction, when this information is an integral part of the address.

e.label: Postal code
e.description: Alphanumeric code assigned the postal delivery area by a national postal agency.

f.label: Title preceding attention name
f.description: Title associated with the attention name (e.g., General, Dr., Reverend) when the title precedes the name.

g.label: Attention name
g.description: Attention name, e.g., the name of a person when an item is to be sent to the attention of a particular person.

h.label: Title following attention name
h.description: Title associated with the attention name (e.g., M.D.) when the title follows the name of the person.

i.label: Type of address
i.description:
One or more words denoting the kind of address found in the field (e.g., " Billing").

First subfield in the field when no subfield $6 is present.

j.label: Specialized telephone number
j.description:
Service number (e.g., a hotline number) other than the administrative or other number contained in subfield $k, $l, or $n.

Examples of specialized telephone numbers include hotline numbers, toll-free "800" numbers, emergency numbers, etc. If more than one specialized telephone number is associated with the address, each number is given in a separate subfield $j. Hotline numbers precede other specialized telephone numbers.

k.label: Telephone number
k.description: Regular telephone number associated with the address and/or the public information contact person at that address. It can also contain information that no telephone number is available. If more than one telephone number is associated with the address and/or public information contact person, each number is given in a separate subfield $k.

l.label: Fax number
l.description: Fax number associated with the address. If more than one fax number is associated with the address, each number is given in a separate subfield $l.

m.label: Electronic mail address
m.description: Electronic mail address associated with the address. If more than one electronic mail address is associated with the address, each number is given in a separate subfield $m.

n.label: TDD or TTY number
n.description: TDD or a TTY number associated with the address. If there is both a TDD number and a TTY number (and/or more than one of each) associated with the address, each number is given in a separate subfield $n.

p.label: Contact person
p.description:
Name of a contact person at the address. If more than one contact person is associated with the address, each name is given in a separate subfield $p.

Not used if the contact person is named in subfield $g.

r.label: Hours
r.description:
Hours that access to the address, contact, and or telephone numbers is available.

If the record is for a system or service, the hours it is available are recorded in field 307 (Hours, Etc.). This subfield is only for the hours associated with address information in field 270. Days of the week and global time zone usually accompany the indication of hours.

z.label: Public note
z.description: Note relating to the address information contained in field 270. The note is written in a form that is adequate for public display.

4.label: Relator code
4.description:
MARC code that specifies the relationship between information in field 270 and the item described in the record. Code from: MARC Code Lists for Relators, Sources, Description Conventions .

More than one relator code may be used if there is more than one relationship. The code is given after other information in the field.

6.label: Linkage
6.description:
Data that links fields that are different script representations of each other. Subfield $6 may contain the tag number of an associated field, an occurrence number, a code that identifies the first script encountered in a left-to-right scan of the field, and an indication that the orientation for a display of the field data is right-to-left. A regular (non-880) field may be linked to one or more 880 fields that all contain different script representations of the same data. Subfield $6 is structured as follows:

$6[linking tag]-[occurrence number]/[script identification code]/[field orientation code]

Subfield $6 is always the first subfield in the field.

Descriptions of multiscript records, with examples, are in Appendix C of the MARC 21 Format for Community Information; specifications for field 880 are under that field; specifications for character sets and repertoires for scripts are found in MARC 21 Specifications for Record Structure, Character Sets, and Exchange Media.

Linking tag part contains the tag number of the associated field. This part is followed immediately by a hyphen and the two-digit occurrence number part. A different occurrence number is assigned to each set of associated fields within a single record. The function of an occurrence number is to permit the matching of the associated fields (not to sequence the fields within the record). An occurrence number may be assigned at random for each set of associated fields. An occurrence number of less than two digits is right justified and the unused position contains a zero.

When there is no associated field to which a field 880 is linked, the occurrence number in subfield $6 is 00. It is used if an agency wants to separate scripts in a record. The linking tag part of subfield $6 will contain the tag that the associated regular field would have had if it had existed in the record.

Occurrence number is followed immediately by a slash (/) and the script identification code. This code identifies the alternate script found in the field. The following codes are used:

These codes have been defined based on the MARC-8 coded character set escape sequences defined in accordance with ISO IEC 2022, "Character Code Structure and Extension Techniques" (equivalent to ANSI X3.41, "Code Extension Techniques for Use with 7-bit and 8-bit Character Sets"). The codes are described in MARC character set documentation.

In a Unicode environment, script identification codes may instead be taken from ISO 15924 "Codes for the representation of names of scripts". Either the alphabetic values (consisting of four letters) or the numerical values (consisting of three digits) may be used.

Entire field need not be in the script identified in subfield $6. If more than one script is present in the field, subfield $6 will contain the identification of the first alternate script encountered in a left-to-right scan of the field.

Note also that the script identification code is used in field 880, subfield $6, but this data element is not generally used for subfield $6 of the associated regular field. In the associated field, the data is assumed to be the primary script(s) for the record.

In a MARC record, the contents of field 880 are always recorded in their logical order, from the first character to the last, regardless of field orientation. For a display of the field, the default field orientation is left-to-right. When the field contains text that has a right-to-left orientation, the script identification code is followed by a slash (/) and the field orientation code. The MARC field orientation code for right-to-left scripts is the letter r. The orientation code is only included in fields with right-to-left orientation, since left-to-right orientation is the default orientation in 880 fields. (See MARC 21 Specifications for Record Structure, Character Sets, and Exchange Media for a detailed description of field orientation.)

Note that the orientation code is used in field 880, subfield $6, but this data element is not generally used for subfield $6 of the associated regular field. In the associated field, the data is assumed to be the usual orientation of the primary script(s) for the record.

303.label: Subordinate Entities
303.description:
Subordinate entity specifics, e.g., information as to when a subunit (e.g., a board) of the community information entity meets. The field is used when it is not desirable to create separate records to handle the subordinate entity specifics.

Meeting specifics of the community information entity per se are given in field 307 (Hours, Etc.). Meeting location specifics of the community information entity per se are recorded in field 270 (Address).

c.description: Information as to the location of the subordinate entity, e.g., where a subordinate meeting is to be held.

311.label: Meeting Rooms and Facilities Available
311.description:
Information about meeting rooms or other facilities associated with the community information entity that are available for use by others. Coded availability information may be contained in field 008/11 (Fixed-length Data Elements/Meeting rooms and facilities available).

Other facilities examples are swimming pools, bowling alleys, or theaters. The data in subfields $b-$h, $m, and $p pertain to the meeting room or facility mentioned in subfield $a or to the equipment mentioned in subfield $e if subfield $a is not present. Accommodations for people with disabilities, fees, and other information associated with the community information entity per se can also be found in the 5XX note fields.

a.label: General description of facilities
a.description: Information as to the type of meeting room or facility that is available, e.g., a swimming pool, a baseball field, etc. It may also contain general information regarding space that is available.

b.label: Name and location
b.description: Name of the meeting room or facility that is available and where it is located.

c.label: Physical description
c.description:
Physical description of the meeting room or facility. Capacity information is recorded in subfield $d.

For instance, for a swimming pool, it can contain information as to whether there are lanes for swimming laps; for an auditorium, it can give information as to whether there is a stage, whether the room is carpeted, etc.

d.label: Capacity
d.description: Information as to the capacity of the meeting room or facility.

e.label: Equipment available
e.description: Information as to equipment that is available for use at the community information entity, e.g., slide projectors, blackboards, etc. Information as to equipment that is available for use outside of the community information entity is given in field 312 (Equipment Available).

f.label: Rental fee
f.description: Information as to the fee involved in renting the meeting room, facility, and/or equipment.

g.label: Special restrictions
g.description:
Special restrictions regarding the rental or use of the meeting room, facility, and/or equipment.

For instance, perhaps the facilities and equipment are only available to community groups.

h.label: Accommodations for the disabled
h.description: Information about accommodations for people with disabilities associated with the meeting room, facility, and/or equipment.

m.label: Miscellaneous information
m.description: Information that is not more appropriately contained in another defined subfield.

p.label: Contact person
p.description:
Name of the person or the source to contact for scheduling the use of the meeting room, facility, and/or equipment or for additional information.

See examples under the descriptions of subfields $b and $h.

312.description:
Information about equipment that is available from the community information entity for use outside of the entity. Information about equipment one can use inside the community information entity is given in subfield $e (Equipment available) of field 311 (Meeting Rooms and Facilities Available).

For instance it may give information as to equipment (e.g., a camera) one can rent and take home to use.

a.label: Type of equipment
a.description: Information as to the type of equipment that is available. It may also contain general information regarding equipment that is available for use.

b.label: Brand name
b.description: Brand name, model number, etc. of the equipment.

c.label: Physical description
c.description: Physical description of the equipment.

f.label: Rental fee
f.description: Information as to the fee involved in renting the equipment.

g.label: Special restrictions
g.description:
Special restrictions regarding the rental or use of the equipment. For instance, perhaps the equipment is only available to particular groups.

See examples under the descriptions of subfields $c and $f.

h.label: Accommodations for the disabled
h.description:
Information about accommodations for people with disabilities associated with the equipment. Perhaps special pieces of equipment are available for use by people with disabilities.

See example under the description of subfield $b.

m.label: Miscellaneous information
m.description:
Information that is not more appropriately contained in another defined subfield.

See example under the description of subfield $f.

p.label: Contact person
p.description:
Name of the person or the source to contact for scheduling the use of the equipment or for additional information.

See examples under the descriptions of subfield $c and $f.

6.label: Linkage
6.description:
Data that links fields that are different script representations of each other. Subfield $6 may contain the tag number of an associated field, an occurrence number, a code that identifies the first script encountered in a left-to-right scan of the field, and an indication that the orientation for a display of the field data is right-to-left. A regular (non-880) field may be linked to one or more 880 fields that all contain different script representations of the same data. Subfield $6 is structured as follows:

$6[linking tag]-[occurrence number]/[script identification code]/[field orientation code]

Subfield $6 is always the first subfield in the field.

Descriptions of multiscript records, with examples, are in Appendix C of the MARC 21 Format for Community Information; specifications for field 880 are under that field; specifications for character sets and repertoires for scripts are found in MARC 21 Specifications for Record Structure, Character Sets, and Exchange Media.

Linking tag part contains the tag number of the associated field. This part is followed immediately by a hyphen and the two-digit occurrence number part. A different occurrence number is assigned to each set of associated fields within a single record. The function of an occurrence number is to permit the matching of the associated fields (not to sequence the fields within the record). An occurrence number may be assigned at random for each set of associated fields. An occurrence number of less than two digits is right justified and the unused position contains a zero.

When there is no associated field to which a field 880 is linked, the occurrence number in subfield $6 is 00. It is used if an agency wants to separate scripts in a record. The linking tag part of subfield $6 will contain the tag that the associated regular field would have had if it had existed in the record.

Occurrence number is followed immediately by a slash (/) and the script identification code. This code identifies the alternate script found in the field. The following codes are used:

These codes have been defined based on the MARC-8 coded character set escape sequences defined in accordance with ISO IEC 2022, "Character Code Structure and Extension Techniques" (equivalent to ANSI X3.41, "Code Extension Techniques for Use with 7-bit and 8-bit Character Sets"). The codes are described in MARC character set documentation.

In a Unicode environment, script identification codes may instead be taken from ISO 15924 "Codes for the representation of names of scripts". Either the alphabetic values (consisting of four letters) or the numerical values (consisting of three digits) may be used.

Entire field need not be in the script identified in subfield $6. If more than one script is present in the field, subfield $6 will contain the identification of the first alternate script encountered in a left-to-right scan of the field.

Note also that the script identification code is used in field 880, subfield $6, but this data element is not generally used for subfield $6 of the associated regular field. In the associated field, the data is assumed to be the primary script(s) for the record.

In a MARC record, the contents of field 880 are always recorded in their logical order, from the first character to the last, regardless of field orientation. For a display of the field, the default field orientation is left-to-right. When the field contains text that has a right-to-left orientation, the script identification code is followed by a slash (/) and the field orientation code. The MARC field orientation code for right-to-left scripts is the letter r. The orientation code is only included in fields with right-to-left orientation, since left-to-right orientation is the default orientation in 880 fields. (See MARC 21 Specifications for Record Structure, Character Sets, and Exchange Media for a detailed description of field orientation.)

Note that the orientation code is used in field 880, subfield $6, but this data element is not generally used for subfield $6 of the associated regular field. In the associated field, the data is assumed to be the usual orientation of the primary script(s) for the record.

8.label: Field link and sequence number
8.description:
Data that identifies linked fields and may also propose a sequence for the linked fields. Subfield $8 may be repeated to link a field to more than one other group of fields. The structure and syntax for the field link and sequence number subfield is:

$8[linking number].[sequence number]\[field link type]

Linking number is the first data element in the subfield and required if the subfield is used. It is a variable-length whole number that occurs in subfield $8 in all fields that are to be linked. Fields with the same linking number are considered linked.

Sequence number is separated from linking number by a period "." and is optional. It is a variable- length whole number that may be used to indicate the relative order for display of the linked fields (lower sequence numbers displaying before higher ones). If it is used it must occur in all $8 subfields containing the same linking number.

Field link type is separated from preceding data by a reverse slash "\". It is a code indicating the reason for the link and it follows the link number, or sequence number if present. The following one-character field link type codes have been defined for use in subfield $8:

p.label: Metadata provenance
p.description: Used in a record to link a field with another field containing information about provenance of the metadata recorded in the linked field.

u.label: General linking, type unspecified
u.description: Used in cases when a specific link type is not appropriate. Code “u” may serve as a default value when there is no information about the reason for the link available.

440.label: Series Title
440.description: Name of a series when an event is part of a series.

indicator1.label: Undefined
indicator1.description: Undefined and contains a blank (#).

indicator2.label: Nonfiling characters
indicator2.description: Value that specifies the number of character positions associated with a definite or indefinite article (e.g., The, An) at the beginning of a series title that are disregarded in sorting and filing processes.

0.label: No nonfiling characters present
0.description:
No initial article character positions are disregarded.

Diacritical marks or special characters at the beginning of a series title field that does not begin with an initial article are not counted as nonfiling characters.

1-9.label: Number of nonfiling characters present
1-9.description: A non-zero value indicates that a title begins with a definite or indefinite article that is disregarded in sorting and filing processes. Any diacritical mark, space or mark of punctuation associated with the article and any space or mark of punctuation preceding the first filing character after the article is included in the count of nonfiling characters. Any diacritic, however, associated with the first filing character is not included in the count of nonfiling characters.

a.label: Title
a.description: Series title, exclusive of any name or number of a part/section.

n.label: Number of part/section
n.description: Number designation for a part/section of a series title. Numbering is defined as an indication of sequencing in any form, e.g., Part 1, Section A.

p.label: Name of part/section
p.description: Name designation of a part/section of a series title.

v.label: Sequential designation
v.description: Sequential designation associated with the series.

Occurrence number is followed immediately by a slash (/) and the script identification code. This code identifies the alternate script found in the field. The following codes are used:

These codes have been defined based on the MARC-8 coded character set escape sequences defined in accordance with ISO IEC 2022, "Character Code Structure and Extension Techniques" (equivalent to ANSI X3.41, "Code Extension Techniques for Use with 7-bit and 8-bit Character Sets"). The codes are described in MARC character set documentation.

In a Unicode environment, script identification codes may instead be taken from ISO 15924 "Codes for the representation of names of scripts". Either the alphabetic values (consisting of four letters) or the numerical values (consisting of three digits) may be used.

Entire field need not be in the script identified in subfield $6. If more than one script is present in the field, subfield $6 will contain the identification of the first alternate script encountered in a left-to-right scan of the field.

Note also that the script identification code is used in field 880, subfield $6, but this data element is not generally used for subfield $6 of the associated regular field. In the associated field, the data is assumed to be the primary script(s) for the record.

In a MARC record, the contents of field 880 are always recorded in their logical order, from the first character to the last, regardless of field orientation. For a display of the field, the default field orientation is left-to-right. When the field contains text that has a right-to-left orientation, the script identification code is followed by a slash (/) and the field orientation code. The MARC field orientation code for right-to-left scripts is the letter r. The orientation code is only included in fields with right-to-left orientation, since left-to-right orientation is the default orientation in 880 fields. (See MARC 21 Specifications for Record Structure, Character Sets, and Exchange Media for a detailed description of field orientation.)
